h.strategy: Aim for hypotheses you believe are about 60-75% likely to hold but that a careful expert would call uncertain: conditional effects rather than main effects. Good sources are diminishing returns (an improving edit helps less when the parent already has a similar strong component), damage concentration (a harmful edit hurts more when the parent has few alternative routes or little spare capacity), and asymmetry (adding a capability and removing it need not have mirror-image effects). Each hypothesis should name the mechanism in one sentence. Avoid claims that are merely definitional or true by construction, and avoid claims that need an unusual sign reversal to be true.

hyps.why: A strong direct input-to-output conv adds less when a strong conv path through node 1 already supplies similar capacity.
Removing edge 0 hurts more when the direct 0->3 route is absent, leaving few alternative paths.
Cutting the node-2 output route hurts more when no direct route into the output exists.
With edge 5 absent, edge 4 is a main route into the output, so removing it risks disconnection and a large drop.
Replacing an empty edge with a skip is a gain, whereas replacing a conv with a skip is a loss.
Filling a removed edge 0 with a conv gains far more than upgrading an existing operation.
A strong direct route into node 2 substitutes for the removed route through node 1, so the removal hurts less.
If node 2 cannot reach the output directly, edge 1 barely matters, so pooling costs less than when edge 1 carries a live path.
A strong direct convolution already provides much of the capacity, so a further conv on edge 5 adds less.
A strong conv at node 2 carries the output, so losing the direct path costs less.
